newsitem.title: USA: House passes bill to give workers comp time option.
newsitem.headline: House passes bill to give workers comp time option.

text.p: The House Wednesday voted to let American workers take time off in lieu of overtime pay, a move Republicans called family friendly and President Clinton termed a threat to fair labor laws, which he is certain to veto.

By a largely party-line vote of 222-210 lawmakers approved legislation to alter a 1938 labor law that now requires private businesses to provide overtime pay for most employees who work more than 40 hours a week. Public sector workers already have the option of choosing compensatory time instead of overtime pay.
Republican leaders and businesses have made the measure a priority, saying it would give hard-pressed working parents much-needed flexibility to spend time with their families.
Democrats and their union allies charged the bill undermined vital labor protections and would let businesses bully employees into working extra hours without extra pay.

The Senate is expected to take up a similar measure later this spring, but unless there is a political breakthrough the measure is unlikely to become law. The House margin of support was far short of the two-thirds majority needed to override a veto.

The Working Families Flexibility Act would let private- sector businesses give their workers the option of taking one-and-one-half hours of paid time off, or comp time, instead of wages for overtime pay.
